claim: The EndpointPickerConfig plugins list injects a comprehensive set of defaults when omitted, including metrics-data-source and core-metrics-extractor for the DataLayer, and per-signal DataProducers (token-producer, approx-prefix-cache-producer, mm-embeddings-cache-producer, inflight-load-producer, predicted-latency-producer, session-id-producer) -- so a non-k8s-backend router must either satisfy or explicitly override each of these default wiring points.
stance_target: the concrete set of default plugin wiring a custom-backend implementation has to account for
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo, docs/architecture.md, as of Aug 25 2026 commit
quoted_support: DataLayer: metrics-data-source and core-metrics-extractor are injected and wired together. Skipped when dataLayer.injectDefaults is false, or when the config's own dataLayer.sources already lists a metrics-data-source entry.

claim: Global Screener plugins run once per request before any scheduling profile and are intersected across independently-filtered candidate sets; docs recommend implementing a scheduling Filter instead of a Screener unless a constraint must apply to every profile -- this is the mandatory-vs-optional filtering distinction relevant to designing a non-pod-backend filter.
stance_target: correct plugin type (Screener vs Filter) to use when adding backend-selection logic
quoted_support: Each screener receives an independent copy of the same endpoint set, and their returned subsets are intersected. Most endpoint-selection plugins should implement a scheduling Filter, not a Screener.

claim: The Data Layer follows a Source -> Extract -> Attribute lifecycle where 'Data sources collect per-endpoint data. Some poll pods periodically, ... others react to endpoint or Kubernetes object change notifications' -- explicitly naming polling (pluggable transport, engine-agnostic) versus Kubernetes-object-reaction (pod-watch specific) as two distinct DataSource strategies already supported.
stance_target: identifying the DataSource abstraction as the extension point for non-k8s endpoint discovery/metrics
scope_conditions: llm-d-router architecture.md, Metric Scraping and the Data Layer section
quoted_support: Data sources collect per-endpoint data. Some poll pods periodically, for metrics ... or served models and LoRA adapters (via /v1/models); others react to endpoint or Kubernetes object change notifications

claim: Polling DataSource plugins share one Collector goroutine per endpoint, ticking off a global base interval set by --refresh-metrics-interval (default 50ms); each plugin's own interval parameter is rounded to the nearest multiple of that base tick.
stance_target: runtime/perf characteristics a custom polling DataSource for a non-pod backend must fit into
quoted_support: Polling sources share one Collector goroutine per endpoint. The base tick is --refresh-metrics-interval (default 50ms).

claim: The current llm-d-router architecture explicitly states a hard assumption of a single InferencePool and single EPP 'due to Envoy limitations', and that only one base model per InferencePool is supported (multiple models require multiple InferencePools) -- both constraints independent of the backend-type question but relevant to overall deployment topology for a customized router.
stance_target: known architectural limits unrelated to but co-located with the pod-backend question
quoted_support: Single InferencePool and single EPP due to Envoy limitations ... Currently only one base model per InferencePool is supported. Multiple models are supported via multiple InferencePools.

claim: Feature gates can be set via a --feature-gates CLI flag using kubelet-style name=bool entries (a bare name enables the gate), and these CLI-supplied gates are applied after, and therefore override, the configuration YAML's own featureGates list.
stance_target: precedence rule between CLI flags and YAML config for feature gates
quoted_support: Feature gates can also be set with the --feature-gates command line argument, which takes a comma-separated list of kubelet-style name=bool entries; a bare name enables the gate. These entries are applied after the configuration's own featureGates list, so they override it.
